> 「受持读诵此经，若为人轻贱，是人先世罪业，应堕恶道，以今世人轻贱故，先世罪业则为消灭。」

Section sixteen makes a claim that has caused a great deal of quiet harm, and the book spends most of its commentary on the boundary of that claim.

The claim: someone who receives and holds this sutra, and is then treated with contempt — mocked, dismissed, pushed aside — has that contempt count against old karma. What would have ripened as a heavy fall has ripened, in this life, as a lighter thing. 重业轻受.

## What the claim does not license

The misreading is common and it is dangerous: *being mistreated is clearing my debt, so I should accept mistreatment, and so should others.*

The book is explicit that this is wrong on both sides. Karma ripening is a description of how consequences appear; it does not make the abuse appropriate. One may defend oneself, name the harm, leave, resist. What the section addresses is the inner position — the hatred, the ledger, the identity of the wronged — and even that is not commanded to be absent by force.

Applied socially, the doctrine of suffering-as-purification becomes an instrument for keeping people in place. That is not the sutra's intent, and the commentary says so.

## 轻贱 is the specific case

Note what kind of difficulty is named. Not illness, not loss, not disaster: contempt. Being looked down on. The particular pain of being thought small.

That is chosen because it is the most common experience of anyone who holds an unpopular view, and because it targets exactly the mark this sutra dissolves — the self that needs to be respected.

## The comparison with 供养诸佛

The Buddha then measures himself: for aeons before 然灯佛, he served eight hundred and forty million亿 nayutas of buddhas, without missing one. Every offering made.

Then: someone in a later age who receives and reads this sutra, their merit exceeds that, by a factor that cannot be expressed.

The point is not self-deprecation. It is that serving an infinite number of teachers is still a relation between a server and a served — the structure the sutra is dismantling. Whereas receiving this text removes the structure.

## 果报不可思议 has a specific meaning

In Chinese popular usage, 不可思议 has drifted into "miraculous, granting wishes". The section's own sentence continues differently: if the Buddha described this merit in full, some people would not believe it, and would be harmed by their disbelief.

Which is a statement about the limits of description, not about the availability of favours. The merit is outside the accounting frame; that is why describing it fully would break the frame rather than inform it.

## The test

Think of a time you were dismissed. Not the worst — an ordinary one, recent.

Then separate three layers:

- The event: what was actually said or done.
- The response: what you did about it.
- The keeping: what still turns over when you remember.

The section's claim concerns the third. The first two remain entirely yours to act on, and acting on them is not a failure of patience.
